clue.text: Someone who brought Oscar home protects distressed Grouch with prayer

indicators.note: something distressed is knocked out of shape, so the letters are thrown into a new order
to protect something is to wrap yourself around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the singer won the Best Actress Oscar for Moonstruck
the six letters of grouch rearranged

explanation.surface: Oscar the Grouch, Sesame Street's trash-can dweller, gets taken home and wrapped in a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' and 'Grouch' together summon the Sesame Street muppet, but the Oscar here is the film award, and CHER wraps around the jumbled GROUCH to make CHURCHGOER. 'Prayer' is read as one who prays.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchgoer attends services to worship, so they are someone who prays: a prayer in the sense of a person, not the words.

clue.text: To begin with, children (1–17, e.g.) should never be put in these!

definitions.text: children (1–17, e.g.) should never be put in these

indicators.note: the opening of the next word is used, its first letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of children
one to seventeen are examples of ages

explanation.surface: A protest that children of any age must never be locked up in these.
explanation.walkthrough: '1–17, e.g.' looks like a cross-reference to other clues, but it is the span of children's ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Cages are barred enclosures for animals, and a protest against caging migrant children is the reference.

clue.text: Start to undermine monarch with, um, the makings of a nuclear weapon

definitions.text: the makings of a nuclear weapon

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of undermine
a rani is an Indian queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruler's hesitant 'um' gives away plans for a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: A rani is a Hindu queen or a raja's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Enriched uranium is the fissile material in atomic bombs, so it is the raw material for them.

clue.text: Replicate and recombine 28s of monastic breakfast food

indicators.note: copying the pieces and then mixing them builds a new arrangement from repeated letters

parts.note: the ingredients of monastic are its letters; copied where needed and remixed they make two words

explanation.surface: Monks' morning meal is copied and reconstituted, like a lab experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is INGREDIENT, so '28s of monastic' are its letters. Uses only letters of MONASTIC, some repeated (N three times, A, O and T twice), which is why the clue says replicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon toast is buttered toast sprinkled with sugar and cinnamon, eaten in the morning.

clue.text: This might help you make strategic decisions: infuse egg, for instance, with hydrogen or yttrium

definitions.text: This might help you make strategic decisions

indicators.note: to infuse something is to put another substance into it

parts.note: an egg is an example of a reproductive cell
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
taken as written
Y is the chemical symbol for yttrium

explanation.surface: A recipe: steep an egg in hydrogen or yttrium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infuse egg ... with hydrogen' puts H inside GAMETE, between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Game theory is the mathematics of choices made against rational opponents, used to plan strategy.

clue.text: Puppet made from wood and love

parts.note: elm is a wood
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Pinocchio-like, a puppet carved from wood and loved.
explanation.walkthrough: Elmo is the red Sesame Street muppet.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmo is a Sesame Street muppet, and a muppet is a kind of puppet.

clue.text: Cautious women, we hear, concealing a summer activity

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken form of the phrase, not its spelling
the spoken phrase keeps the answer tucked inside its run of sounds, across the word break

parts.note: said out loud, women sounds like wimmin, and the end of cautious runs into it

explanation.surface: Wary women at the beach keep a summer pastime under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'women' sounds like 'wimmin', so the end of 'cautious' and the start of 'women' run together as SWIM. The letters on the page do not spell it; only the sounds do.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming is a typical warm-weather pastime, so a swim is a summer activity by example.

clue.text: Unfinished card game, according to rumor

indicators.note: unfinished means the game's name stops before its last letter

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
per means according to, as in per the rules

explanation.surface: A card game abandoned partway, as gossip reports it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to rumor' reads as one phrase, but 'according to' is wordplay and 'rumor' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisper can be a rumor or hint passed quietly from person to person.

clue.text: German octet pursuing me with carefree luxury craft

parts.note: taken as written
gay in its older sense of lighthearted
acht is German for eight

explanation.surface: Eight Germans chase me on a carefree pleasure boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is used in its older sense of lighthearted, and 'pursuing' means the German word comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A megayacht is an enormous private yacht, a luxury vessel for the very rich.

clue.text: Profit involving a share of rye or barley, perhaps

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a profit is a gain

indicators.note: only a portion is taken, here the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of rye

explanation.surface: A farmer's profit comes partly from rye or barley sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rye' is used twice over: its first letter goes inside GAIN, and it also starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye and barley are both cereal crops, examples of grain; the 'perhaps' flags them as examples.

clue.text: Tapestry artist following G. Puccini character's imitation

definitions.note: a noun defining a verbal noun in -ing

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of La Bohème, by Giacomo (G.) Puccini
Carole King recorded the album Tapestry; as C. King she supplies these letters

explanation.surface: A weaver copies a Puccini heroine onto a tapestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tapestry artist' looks like a weaver, but Tapestry is Carole King's 1971 album, and she is taken as C. KING. 'Following G. Puccini character' places her after MIMI, from La Bohème.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicking is the act of copying someone, which is the same thing as imitation.

clue.text: Sing about spy, poet, and actress

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organization
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A celebrity sings about a spy, a poet and an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the subject of', but it turns MOLE backwards. Carole Lombard was a 1930s Hollywood comedy star.
explanation.definitionFit: Carole Lombard starred in screwball comedies such as My Man Godfrey, so she is an actress.

clue.text: What you might wear on the slopes to bypass bugs

definitions.text: What you might wear on the slopes

parts.note: to skip something is to bypass it
ants are bugs (insects)

explanation.surface: Choosing clothing for the ski slopes that keeps insects away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening phrase; 'to' joins it to SKIP and ANTS, which read as SKI PANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are the warm waterproof trousers worn by skiers, so they are clothing for the slopes.

clue.text: Ask probing questions about federal organization, and settle early

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to pry is to ask nosy questions
the Environmental Protection Agency, a US federal body

explanation.surface: Grilling a federal agency, then paying off a debt ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The EPA is the US Environmental Protection Agency.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepay a bill is to pay it before it is due, which is settling it early.

clue.text: Relative redistributed letters from priest

indicators.note: handing out again in a new pattern, so the letters are reused in a fresh order

parts.note: only letters found in priest are used, some more than once

explanation.surface: A family member hands out a clergyman's mail.
explanation.walkthrough: As in 3 down, the letters of PRIEST are reused rather than shuffled once: STEP and SISTER are each spelt from them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepsister is the daughter of a step-parent, a family member by marriage.

clue.text: Drowsy moon's terribly advanced

indicators.note: done terribly means done badly and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of moons rearranged
money advanced is money lent

explanation.surface: A sleepy moon has moved terribly far forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon's' looks like a possessive, but it is the five letters MOONS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent describes someone sleepy or inclined to doze, a formal synonym for drowsy.

clue.text: Thus, a boner pill originally terrified Bernie Sanders, for example

parts.note: so means thus
Cialis is a brand of erectile dysfunction drug

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its opening, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of terrified

explanation.surface: A senator panicked by an impotence drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Cialis is a US erectile dysfunction drug, like Viagra.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernie Sanders describes himself as a democratic socialist, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Singable clip taken from ghastly rickroll

indicators.note: the answer is lifted out of the words that follow, sitting in them unchanged

parts.note: the tail of ghastly joined to the head of rickroll

explanation.surface: A snippet from a dreadful Rick Astley prank video that you can sing along to.
explanation.walkthrough: A rickroll is the internet prank of linking someone to Rick Astley's 'Never Gonna Give You Up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a line of song words, a short piece of text meant to be sung.

clue.text: Spoken instructions on how to turn 2 into 8 (or 18) inches

indicators.note: the instruction is said out loud, and the answer is spelt as the sounds suggest

parts.words: instructions on how to turn 2 into 8
parts.note: two multiplied by itself three times is eight, so the instruction is to raise 2 to the third power

explanation.surface: Told out loud how to change one number into another, with a length in inches tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is split across the clue: '8 (or 18) inches' reads as eight inches, but the cubit is the 18-inch measure, and the 2 and 8 belong to the arithmetic of 'cube it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cubit is an ancient length measure based on the forearm, usually reckoned at about eighteen inches.

clue.text: Drag Affleck to Reverend Spooner — that's where you might get some relief

definitions.text: where you might get some relief

indicators.note: William Spooner was famous for swapping the first sounds of words, so the opening sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: to pull is to drag; the word is taken by its sound, the opening P to be swapped
Ben Affleck is the American actor

explanation.surface: Hauling a Hollywood actor over to meet a famous Oxford clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To Reverend Spooner' swaps the opening sounds, so PULL BEN becomes BULL PEN. In baseball the bullpen is where relief pitchers warm up, hence the relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullpen is the area where relief pitchers warm up before entering a baseball game.

clue.text: Obnoxious agent beginning to tweet after talk show

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the others in the line

parts.note: a rep is a representative, an agent
Ellen DeGeneres's daytime US talk show was called Ellen

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of tweet

explanation.surface: A nasty publicist sends a tweet straight after a talk-show appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obnoxious agent' looks like one phrase, but only 'Obnoxious' defines; 'agent' gives REP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent provokes disgust, so it is offensive or obnoxious.

clue.text: Weave tangled net at port, say

indicators.note: a tangled thing is knotted out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of net rearranged
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A fisherman weaves a knotted net in a harbor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like a harbor, but 'say' marks it as an example of WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist strands together, which is to weave them.

clue.text: Look at area in the back of the boat, staying on top of water

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside another

parts.note: aft is the rear part of a ship
lo is an old word meaning look
A is the abbreviation for area; at is a link inside the wordplay

explanation.surface: Someone looks at the area at the stern of a boat that is still floating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back of the boat' looks like it should be STERN, but the short nautical word is needed; 'lo' is the archaic 'look!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Afloat means floating on the surface rather than sinking, which is staying on top of water.

clue.text: Tautology juxtaposed with random chat? That doesn't go together

indicators.note: random means in no set order, so the letters are reshuffled
placed side by side, so the pieces are joined end to end

parts.note: M is M is a statement that is true by repeating itself
the letters of chat rearranged

explanation.surface: A pointless repetition sits beside idle chatter, and the two clash.
explanation.walkthrough: A tautology says the same thing twice; 'M is M' is a model one, giving MISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A mismatch is a pairing of things that fail to suit each other, things that do not go together.

clue.text: Spook hits on family member

parts.note: H is the scorecard abbreviation for hits in baseball
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A spy makes a pass at a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spook' looks like a noun for a spy or a ghost, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone is to frighten them as a ghost does, which is to spook them.

clue.text: Coward backs Trotsky

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is read from its end

parts.note: the playwright Noël Coward

explanation.surface: A timid person supports a Russian revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person, but it is the English playwright Noël Coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was the Russian revolutionary leader, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: Hospital resident with terrible pain and connection to nephrologist, marginally

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the letters of pain rearranged
a tie is a link or connection

indicators.note: the margins of a word are its outer edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of nephrologist

explanation.surface: A hospital patient in terrible pain is linked up with a kidney specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: A nephrologist is a kidney doctor, which keeps the hospital picture going while giving only its edges.
explanation.definitionFit: An inpatient stays in hospital overnight or longer, so lives there for a while as a resident.

clue.text: Farewell, gold-plated pass

indicators.note: plating covers something on the outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye while handing over a gold-plated ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold-plated' looks like one adjective, but it is split: 'gold' gives the letters and 'plated' tells you they go round 'pass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, borrowed into English as a parting word.

clue.text: A lunatic flips over fish

indicators.note: flipping over turns things back to front, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A madman turns somersaults over a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A and NUT are joined, then the whole run is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a large ocean fish, a common example of the class.

clue.text: Component of tire ending in a mess

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the ten letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A worn-out tire part ends up all over the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Component of tire' wants to be the definition, but only 'Component' defines; 'of' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one of the parts that make up a mixture, which is a component.
